newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny may decide to shed businesses.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny may decide to shed businesses.

text.p: Allegheny Teledyne Inc will decide during the next several months whether to sell at least some of its non-specialty metal businesses, Richard P. Simmons, chairman, president, and chief executive officer, said Tuesday.
"No decisions have been made yet," he said. "I think the board will make judgments over the next coming months (on possible sales.")
Simmons made his comments at a news conference that marked the official opening of the company's new corporate headquarters in downtown Pittsburgh.
Allegheny Teledyne was formed in August by the merger of the former Allegheny Ludlum Corp, the nation's largest flat-rolled specialty steelmaker, and Los Angeles-based Teledyne Inc.

The company has annual revenues of about $3.8 billion. Following the merger, some Wall Street analysts said they expected the company to eventually sell some or all of the non-specialty metals businesses that belonged to Teledyne Inc, including aviation, electronics and consumer products.
Tuesday marked the first time since the merger that Simmons has indicated that businesses may be sold. In prior comments, Simmons had said there were no such plans.
He said the board will be evaluating non-specialty metal businesses over the next several months and deciding whether they have the "critical mass" to compete in their respective markets.
"They also will look at whether they fit strategically with Allegheny Teledyne's long-term plan and opportunities for growth," he said.
